slot.brief: Compare [Fe(CN)6]4− and [Fe(H2O)6]2+ for hybridisation and magnetic nature (diamagnetic vs paramagnetic); pick the correct pairing.

stem: Which pairing correctly describes $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$, respectively?

verdicts.working: Fe²⁺ is d⁶. CN⁻ gives a low-spin inner-orbital complex (d²sp³), diamagnetic; H₂O gives a high-spin outer-orbital complex (sp³d²), paramagnetic.

working:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $d^6$.\
$\text{CN}^-$ is strong-field: low-spin $d^6$, $d^2sp^3$, 0 unpaired electrons.\
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is weak-field: high-spin $d^6$, $sp^3d^2$, 4 unpaired electrons.

Independent check: Fe²⁺ is d⁶. CN⁻ gives a low-spin inner-orbital complex (d²sp³), diamagnetic; H₂O gives a high-spin outer-orbital complex (sp³d²), paramagnetic.
solution:
Fe$^{2+}$ has configuration $3d^6$. CN$^-$ is a strong-field ligand, so the complex is low-spin and uses inner $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation; all electrons are paired.
H$_2$O is a weak-field ligand, giving a high-spin $sp^3d^2$ complex with four unpaired electrons.
Thus, the pair is $d^2sp^3$, diamagnetic; $sp^3d^2$, paramagnetic.
